name: Active
classification_notes: A hand-lettered brush script with automatic ligatures and fill variants, placing it in the script category rather than a formal text face.
summary: A set of six inky brush-script styles built for packaging, branding and posters rather than body text.
description: Active brings a hand-drawn, textured brush feel across three related styles (One, Regular, Two), each available as an outline or solid fill. Automatic ligatures replace repeating letters for a more convincingly hand-lettered look, and stylistic alternates cover some capitals.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design call Active 'a set of six playful and personable inky brush script styles' that work well for packaging, branding, merchandise and posters, with automatic ligatures and bonus OpenType catchwords and ornaments.

name: Bakerie
classification_notes: Modelled on brush-pen handwriting rather than a formal letterform structure, so it sits in the script category despite having a full weight range.
summary: A brush-pen handwritten script running from Thin to Heavy across smooth and rough renderings, with condensed and wide widths.
description: Bakerie was drawn by hand with a brush pen and comes in matching Smooth and Rough finishes, each spanning seven weights and three widths. Stylistic alternates, ligatures and swashes keep it feeling handwritten across sizes.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Bakerie as 'an authentically handwritten script family created by brush pen on paper, designed to be readable, even in smaller sizes,' comprising 42 fonts across weights, widths and rough/smooth finishes.

name: Botany
classification_notes: A hand-drawn serif with embellished capitals built for display use, with a companion Text cut for smaller sizes; the decorative flourish keeps it in display rather than text serif territory.
summary: A hand-drawn display serif with embellished capitals, paired with a plainer Botany Text cut for smaller sizes.
description: Botany leans on uniquely decorated capitals for a natural, elegant character at display sizes. Botany Text strips back the embellishment for use in body copy, and both cuts come with italics.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design call Botany 'a distinctly hand-drawn display serif with an optional decorative flourish,' noting its 'uniquely embellished capitals that evoke a kind of natural elegance,' suited to landscaping and organic packaging work.

name: Braisetto
classification_notes: A handwritten script with a five-weight range, unusual for the category but still built from a single continuous hand gesture rather than a constructed letterform.
summary: A jovial handwritten script running from Thin to Black, built to work in both a supporting and a lead display role.
description: Braisetto keeps an inky, expressive handwritten character across five weights, giving it more range than most scripts. Adam Ladd Design position it for branding, packaging, display and product work.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Braisetto 'a jovial script typeface designed with a handwritten exuberance...inky and readable, expressive and functional...thoughtfully designed to be both individual and versatile at the same time.'

name: Cheddar Gothic
subcategory: rough-hewn gothic sans (superfamily with serif/slab/stencil cuts)
classification_notes: The core family is an all-caps rough-hewn gothic sans; companion Serif, Slab and Stencil cuts extend the same skeleton into other categories, but the primary entry is classified by its sans form.
summary: An all-caps, deliberately rough-hewn gothic sans that also spins off matching serif, slab and stencil cuts.
description: Cheddar Gothic is hand-drawn with a rugged, uneven edge, built as an all-caps family across Light to Black. Sans Two adds a companion set of weights, and the wider superfamily includes serif, slab and stencil companions plus catchwords and icons.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Cheddar Gothic as 'a deliberately rough-hewn sans typeface' where 'each style in the family is rugged, readable, and thoughtfully hand-drawn,' aimed at travel branding, urban campaigns and food packaging.

name: Citrus Gothic
classification_notes: An all-caps display gothic with five decorative treatments (inline, rough, shadow, solid, regular), built for headlines rather than text.
summary: A hand-drawn, all-caps gothic sans offered in five decorative treatments from inline to shadow, all with italics.
description: Citrus Gothic keeps a tight, condensed-looking gothic skeleton but adds irregular hand-drawn detail and curled terminals. Solid, texture, inline, rough and shadow versions cover a wide range of headline treatments.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Citrus Gothic 'a distinctly hand-drawn, all-caps gothic sans family' that 'leans on a classic, condensed gothic appearance but adds flair with irregular details and curled terminals.'

name: Config
classification_notes: A circular-featured geometric sans with straight sides, ten weights and a Condensed cut; the rounded tops and bottoms with sturdy straight sides place it firmly in the geometric grotesque space.
summary: A ten-weight geometric sans with circular tops and bottoms and straight sturdy sides, plus a Condensed cut and a variable font.
description: Config draws on industrial geometric sans models, running Thin through Ultra with matching italics. A Condensed width and a weight/width/slant Variable font extend the same skeleton for tighter or more flexible use.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Config as 'a geometric sans family in the style of other industrial typefaces,' with 'circular forms on the tops and bottoms of characters' and 'straight sides for a sturdy and space-saving design,' aiming for an 'efficiently neutral, friendly' result.

name: Config Mono
classification_notes: A fixed-width adaptation of Config, explicitly built as a monospace font for code and UI use.
summary: A fixed-width version of Config aimed at code, UI and captions, with a matching variable font.
description: Config Mono carries the geometric spirit of Config into a monospace format, with subtle refinements to the roman and italic for on-screen reading. Adam Ladd Design suggest it for smaller UI and coding sizes as well as larger editorial use.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Config Mono 'a monospace sans serif, adapting the modern technical spirit of the Config font family into a fixed-width format,' suited to 'UI, coding, game consoles, and captions' as well as magazines and packaging at larger sizes.

name: Config Rounded
classification_notes: The rounded companion to Config, softening the same circular-topped geometric skeleton for a warmer tone.
summary: A soft, rounded geometric sans in ten weights, softening Config's circular geometric skeleton for a warmer feel.
description: Config Rounded keeps Config's circular tops and bottoms and space-saving straight sides but rounds off the details for a friendlier tone, spanning Thin to Black with italics throughout.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Config Rounded as 'a soft geometric sans family in the style of other industrial typefaces' offering 'subtle warmth that still looks modern and strong.'

name: Cut Block
classification_notes: A single-weight geometric display face with a woodcut-style rugged edge, built for headline use rather than text.
summary: A rugged single-weight display face styled after cut woodblock lettering.
description: Cut Block takes the tactile, hand-cut look of woodblock printing and applies it to a 20th-century geometric letterform, aimed at packaging, editorial and event work.
foundry_blurb: The foundry says Cut Block 'vividly brings to life the concept of slicing through wood, evoking a tactile sense of craftsmanship' with 'a rugged aesthetic that draws inspiration from other iconic 20th-century geometric typefaces — albeit with a creative twist.'

name: Farmhand
classification_notes: An all-caps condensed display face offered in both serif and sans versions, classified here under display given its hand-drawn, headline-first design.
summary: A hand-drawn, all-caps condensed display face offered in matching serif and sans cuts.
description: Farmhand pairs a condensed serif with a Farmhand Sans companion, both hand-drawn for a natural, vintage, homemade feel. Inline and italic versions and a set of Extras with alternates and ornaments round out the family.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design call Farmhand 'a hand-drawn all-caps condensed serif and sans family' well suited 'for branding and other graphic design situations where you want to lean into a natural, vintage, or homemade vibe.'

name: Fields
classification_notes: A rounded-serif display face with three optical sizes (Text, Display, Big); its teardrop terminals and casual tone place it in a retro display-serif subcategory.
summary: A casual retro serif with rounded serifs and teardrop terminals, spanning three optical sizes from text to an Ultra-weight Big cut.
description: Fields blends a 1970s vinyl-record warmth with modern proportions across eight weights. A variable font and dedicated Display and Big optical sizes let it scale from body copy to poster-scale headlines.
foundry_blurb: The foundry describes Fields as 'a versatile family with three optical sizes blending casual, retro tones with modern touches,' with 'rounded serifs, teardrop terminals, and subtle tails' for a 'friendly and approachable' feel.

name: Fractul
classification_notes: A large-x-height geometric sans with straightened strokes for an angular, architectural feel; Fractul Alt offers an alternate character set on the same structure.
summary: An architectural geometric sans with a large x-height and straightened strokes for an angular, avant-garde feel, plus an Alt companion.
description: Fractul runs Hairline to Black with italics and comes with variable font versions of both the main family and the Fractul Alt companion. Over 600 glyphs and a broad OpenType feature set support detailed typographic work.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design call Fractul and Fractul Alt 'architectural geometric sans serifs, dramatically modern because of a larger x-height with a more distinct and avant-garde voice — most evident in characters where specific strokes have been straightened for a strong angular appearance.'

name: Fromage
classification_notes: A high-contrast sans with generous x-height and round forms aimed at fashion and luxury branding; Fromage Alt swaps in flat terminals for a different character.
summary: A high-contrast fashion sans with round forms and a generous x-height, offered with angled or flat terminals across seven weights.
description: Fromage balances an elegant, dynamic rhythm against restrained forms, aimed at fashion, beauty and luxury work. Fromage Alt swaps the angled terminals for flat ones, and both come as variable fonts.
foundry_blurb: The foundry describes Fromage and Fromage Alt as 'modern, high-contrast sans serif typefaces that balance the unexpected with restraint,' with 'an elegant air and a dynamic rhythm' for fashion, beauty and luxury branding.

name: Garlic Salt
classification_notes: A hand-drawn monolinear serif with semi-condensed proportions and a large x-height, built to stay legible from display down to small sizes.
summary: A hand-drawn, monolinear serif with semi-condensed proportions and a large x-height, in Regular and Bold with italics.
description: Garlic Salt mixes whimsical and modern qualities in a single-weight-plus-bold serif, with a matching Extras font of ornaments and dingbats for related design work.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Garlic Salt as 'a flavorful, hand-drawn, serif font family with a distinctly monolinear mix of whimsical and modern,' noting its 'large x-height and open counter forms' keep it 'pleasantly readable' at small sizes.

name: Gopher
classification_notes: A geometric sans built on reverse contrast rather than the usual thick-thin pattern, with Text and Display cuts tuning the contrast for different sizes.
summary: A geometric sans with an unusual reverse-contrast structure, tuned across Text, standard and Display optical sizes.
description: Gopher takes a quirky reverse-contrast approach to the geometric sans, with Text offering the most minimal contrast and Display the most dramatic. Eight weights with italics run across all three cuts.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Gopher 'a modernly quirky take on the reverse contrast, geometric sans,' with the three subfamilies varying contrast from Text's minimal treatment to Display's most dramatic.

name: Gopher Mono
classification_notes: The monospace member of the Gopher family, carrying the same reverse-contrast structure into a fixed-width design usable at both text and display sizes.
summary: A monospace take on Gopher's reverse-contrast design, unusual enough to work at display sizes as well as in code.
description: Gopher Mono unites the Gopher superfamily's reverse-contrast look in a fixed-width format across ten weights with italics, positioned for branding and editorial use as much as for code.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design say 'Gopher Mono is a unique take on the monospaced genre with its unexpected reverse contrast design,' noting its quirks 'make it eye-catching for display use' beyond typical monospace applications.

name: Highest Praise
classification_notes: A single-weight, condensed-proportion brush script blending modern and vintage textures.
summary: A bold, condensed brush script with a textured edge, built for quotes, invitations and headline display work.
description: Highest Praise carries swash characters, an alternate 's' and double-letter ligatures, keeping a single expressive weight legible despite its condensed, textured character.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Highest Praise 'a bold and expressive brush script font' with 'condensed proportions and subtle texture on the edges, blending modern and vintage qualities.'

name: Inked Balterm
classification_notes: A single-weight hand-lettered display face with stencil-like construction, built for headline and packaging use.
summary: A hand-lettered display face that dances between thin strokes and solid ball terminals for a stencil-like effect.
description: Inked Balterm carries a playful, hand-drawn charm through its mix of syncopated thin strokes and solid terminals, aimed at media branding, food packaging and travel work.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Inked Balterm as 'the epitome of hand-lettered playful charm' that 'dances between thin syncopated strokes and solid ball terminals,' bringing 'inky charm, demanding attention and sparking creativity.'

name: Inked Classic
classification_notes: An open-face Didone with hand-drawn irregularity, keeping the high-contrast structure of the classification while adding a warmer, less mechanical texture.
summary: An open-face Didone with hand-drawn charm, built to read at small sizes as well as on display work.
description: Inked Classic combines Didone dignity with a hand-drawn warmth, positioned for wine labels and invitations at small sizes and book covers or magazine spreads at display scale.
foundry_blurb: The foundry says Inked Classic 'combines the dignity of a modern openface Didone with hand-drawn charm' and 'evokes nostalgic elegance,' lending 'warmth to typographic circumstances requiring more than cold perfection.'

name: Konnect
classification_notes: A large-x-height geometric sans with closed apertures and horizontal or vertical terminals, built for dramatic display statements.
summary: A geometric sans with a large x-height and closed apertures, built for dramatic branding and advertising statements.
description: Konnect keeps clean, simple forms across nine weights with italics, plus a Weight/Slant variable font, aimed at branding, advertising, logos and headline work.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design call Konnect 'an entirely modern geometric sans made for dramatic statements,' with 'simple, clean forms and proportions' and 'a large x-height, closed apertures, and horizontal/vertical terminals.'

name: Likely
classification_notes: A joyful brush script paired with a hand-lettered sans companion, plus specialty colour, counter, fill and ornament variants; classified as script for its primary hand-drawn gesture.
summary: A joyful brush script paired with Likely Sans, a matching hand-lettered sans, plus colourable specialty variants.
description: Likely and Likely Sans are designed to work together, with Counter, Fill, Shapes and Catchwords variants adding colourisable and decorative options for book jackets, magazine covers and stationery.
foundry_blurb: The foundry describes Likely as 'a joyful brush script family that pairs nicely with Likely Sans, a hand-lettered sans,' designed 'to work together as a naturally vibrant package.'

name: Lufga
classification_notes: A geometric sans distinguished by an unusual double-story g and stemless u, spanning a full ten-weight range with italics.
summary: A geometric sans with a distinctive double-story g and stemless u, running Hairline to Black with a large x-height.
description: Lufga keeps a minimal geometric structure but adds a handful of quirky alternates, giving it more individuality than a typical grotesque. It covers branding, advertising, packaging and web use.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design call Lufga 'a uniquely different, geometric sans serif font family' with 'modern individuality' and 'distinctive alternates,' pointing to 'the unexpectedly unique double-story g and stemless u.'

name: Magdelin
classification_notes: A minimal, low-contrast gothic sans with calligraphic italics that nod to humanist models; semi-condensed proportions and long ascenders give it a vintage cast.
summary: A minimal, low-contrast gothic sans with calligraphic italics, small x-height and long ascenders for a vintage-leaning workhorse.
description: Magdelin pairs simple gothic forms with humanist-style italics across ten weights, plus a Magdelin Alt with an alternate character set. Semi-condensed proportions and long ascenders and descenders set its vintage tone.
foundry_blurb: The foundry describes Magdelin as 'a minimal Gothic sans having simple forms and low contrast' with 'calligraphic details found in the italics' reminiscent of humanist typefaces, calling it 'a valuable, versatile workhorse.'

name: Neato Serif
classification_notes: A hand-drawn, high-contrast serif with theatrical ball terminals; the Rough cut adds surface texture on the same skeleton.
summary: A quirky, high-contrast hand-drawn serif with theatrical ball terminals, in smooth and rough finishes.
description: Neato Serif mixes stately serif proportions with a playful, textured hand and alternates, ligatures and swashes, aimed at magazine headlines, book titles and food packaging.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design call Neato Serif 'a quirky hand-drawn serif family' with 'a unique blend of stately sophistication and playfulness' thanks to its 'textured high contrast and theatrical ball terminals.'

name: Neulis
classification_notes: A three-way superfamily spanning a warm humanist-leaning cut (Neue), a script-flavoured cursive cut, and a dependable geometric sans (Sans); grouped here under sans-serif for its core structure.
summary: A three-part sans superfamily running from a warm Neue cut through a playful script-like Cursive to a dependable geometric Sans.
description: Neulis mixes a geometric sans with a jovial upright script across three related families and six variable fonts, letting designers dial the playfulness up or down while keeping the same underlying structure.
foundry_blurb: The foundry describes the three families as 'a mash-up of a geometric sans serif and jovial upright script,' with Neue 'pleasantly warm,' Cursive 'the most playful — punctuated with script-like letterforms,' and Sans 'geometric and dependable.'

name: Oilvare
classification_notes: A layerable display face built from vintage sign-painting references, with separate shadow, hatch and outline layers meant to be combined.
summary: A hand-drawn, layerable display face inspired by vintage painted signs and oil cans, with matching shadow and outline layers.
description: Oilvare uses wide, oval-inspired forms and medium contrast across four coordinated styles, so shadow and highlight layers can be mixed and matched for painted-sign effects.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Oilvare as 'a hand-drawn, layered family inspired by vintage painted signs and oil cans,' letting users 'mix, match, and layer the styles' via separate highlight and shadow options.

name: Otterco
classification_notes: A theatrical geometric sans referencing early 20th-century models, with a Display cut tightening spacing and width contrast for headlines.
summary: A theatrical, retro-leaning geometric sans, with a Normal cut for text and a tighter Display cut for headlines.
description: Otterco mixes subtly retro details with a starkly modern geometric structure across eight weights. The Display cut narrows spacing and increases width contrast for headline use, while Normal favours captions and larger text settings.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Otterco 'a theatrical geometric sans in the spirit of the early 20th century' that combines 'subtly retro and starkly modern qualities.'

name: Poster Cut Neue
classification_notes: An all-caps display face rooted in historic grotesque sans models but roughened for a hand-cut poster look.
summary: A purposefully rough, all-caps display sans with roots in historic grotesques, built for a hand-cut poster feel.
description: Poster Cut Neue leans on an informal, almost hand-cut construction where uppercase and lowercase differ enough to add movement, suited to grassroots branding, editorial and poster work.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Poster Cut Neue as 'a purposefully rough, hand-drawn display family' rooted in historic grotesque sans typefaces, offering 'an informal, almost hand-cut look and feel.'

name: Quiche
classification_notes: A Didone-influenced design with the serifs removed, keeping the extreme contrast and ball terminals of the genre in a sans structure; classified as sans-serif per the foundry's own framing.
summary: A high-contrast, Didone-influenced sans with ball terminals and angled stems, spread across four coordinated cuts.
description: Quiche strips the serifs from a Didone structure while keeping its extreme contrast and elegance. Display, Fine and Stencil cuts handle dramatic headline work, while Text supports quotes and subheadings.
foundry_blurb: The foundry describes Quiche as 'a high-contrast sans featuring ball terminals and angled stems' influenced by Didone typography, achieving a 'uniquely modern' look 'by removing serifs while maintaining the elegance and extreme contrast' of the genre.

name: Quiche Flare
classification_notes: A high-contrast serif with flared, foxtail terminals and swash capitals, the serif counterpart to the Quiche superfamily.
summary: A high-contrast flared serif with foxtail ball terminals and swash capitals, the serif member of the Quiche family.
description: Quiche Flare adds flared serifs and swash capitals to the Quiche superfamily's high-contrast structure, with a large x-height suited to fashion, packaging and stationery work.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design call Quiche Flare 'a high-contrast, flared serif typeface featuring foxtail ball terminals, swash capitals, and geometric proportions,' offering 'elegance and a touch of whimsy.'

name: Quiche Sans
classification_notes: The standalone sans companion to Quiche and Quiche Flare, using monolinear stroke endings on the same high-contrast Didone-influenced skeleton.
summary: The sans-serif companion to Quiche Flare, pairing monolinear stroke endings with the same high-contrast Didone-influenced proportions.
description: Quiche Sans removes the serifs from the Quiche Flare structure for a cleaner, more modern companion, designed to be mixed with Quiche Flare for extra versatility.
foundry_blurb: The foundry describes Quiche Sans as 'a high-contrast sans with monolinear stroke endings, angled stems, and geometric proportions' influenced by the Didone genre, recommending it be used alongside Quiche Flare 'to expand the versatility even further.'

name: Seabass
classification_notes: A wide sans with slight reverse contrast, built primarily for display use in capitals rather than as a text face.
summary: A wide, modern sans with a slight reverse contrast, drawing on beach and boardwalk culture for display-first use.
description: Seabass leans into an eye-catching wide structure across seven weights and a variable font, working best set in capitals at larger sizes though still usable smaller.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Seabass 'a wide, modern sans serif with slight reverse contrast' that 'blends eye-catching style with function,' drawing on 'skate parks, shopping malls, and boardwalk energy.'

name: Serca
classification_notes: An open-countered grotesque sans built for both text and headline use, with a matching Condensed width and variable font.
summary: An open, precise grotesque sans built to hold up at both text and headline sizes, with a matching Condensed width.
description: Serca stays precise without feeling cold across ten weights and a Condensed companion, with open counters keeping it legible from small text through to large headlines in brand systems and wayfinding.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Serca as 'precise without being cold and modern without being sterile,' with 'open counters and proportions' suited to 'brand systems, wayfinding plans, and marketing strategies.'

name: Skie
classification_notes: A neutral gothic sans offered in normal, condensed and wide widths, giving it grotesque-style versatility across ten weights each.
summary: A neutral gothic sans with a hint of revived charm, offered in normal, Condensed and Wide widths across ten weights.
description: Skie stays understated across sixty fonts split between its normal, Condensed and Wide widths, aimed at branding, publishing and marketing work that needs a quiet, dependable sans.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Skie 'an inconspicuously alluring gothic sans standing apart from the crowd,' achieving 'a neutral appearance, blending modern aesthetics with a hint of revived charm.'

name: Tape Back
classification_notes: An angular, deliberately irregular display face across three weights, built for poster and concert-flyer work rather than text.
summary: A defiantly angular, punk-flavoured display face across Light, Regular and Bold, built for posters and flyers.
description: Tape Back leans into calculated irregularity and freehand placement, positioned for concert posters and eccentric art-show invitations rather than conventional branding.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Tape Back as 'equal parts punk rock and weird science...a fiercely defiant collection of letters working together in a calculated rebellion of angular shapes and freehand placement.'

name: Trailmade
classification_notes: A hand-lettered brush script with a full alternate lowercase set and a companion Extras font of ornaments.
summary: A rugged, hand-lettered brush script with a second set of stylistic alternates and a companion Extras font of dingbats.
description: Trailmade was drawn with a brush pen on paper and carries swashes, ligatures and a complete alternate lowercase for a more varied hand-lettered feel, with an Extras font adding lines and dingbats.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Trailmade 'a rugged and stylish brush script ready to explore an adventurous path,' with 'swashes, ligatures, and a complete second set of lowercase stylistic alternates.'

name: Zuume
classification_notes: A tightly spaced headline sans built for stacking and impact rather than text; the Cut variant adds sliced segments for extra aggression.
summary: A sharp, tightly spaced headline sans built for stacking, with a Cut variant that slices segments out of the letterforms.
description: Zuume is built to invigorate magazine headlines and packaging with a technical, punchy feel, and Zuume Cut adds sliced-out segments for extra movement and speed. Both come as variable fonts.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design say these fonts are 'built to invigorate magazine headlines, media brands, fitness packaging, in-your-face entertainment' with 'a sharp, technical feel that looks great, tightly spaced, and stacked for a visual punch.'

name: Zuume Edge
classification_notes: A mechanical-feeling variant within the Zuume family, again offered with a segmented Cut companion for extra aggression.
summary: A sharp, mechanical-feeling headline sans from the Zuume family, with a segmented Cut companion.
description: Zuume Edge shares the Zuume superfamily's tightly spaced, stacked structure with a harder mechanical edge, and its Cut companion slices out segments for added movement.
foundry_blurb: The foundry describes Zuume Edge as having 'a sharp, mechanical feel' that works well 'tightly spaced and stacked for a visual punch,' with the Cut variant creating 'more movement, aggression, and willful speed.'

name: Zuume Rough
classification_notes: A texturised condensed sans within the Zuume family, kept to two weights but distinguished by its rough surface treatment.
summary: A texturised, condensed sans in just two weights, built to feel tactile and attention-grabbing at headline sizes.
description: Zuume Rough carries a visceral surface texture on a condensed structure, aimed at food packaging, sports entertainment and concert graphics where a raw, physical feel is wanted.
foundry_blurb: Adam Ladd Design describe Zuume Rough as 'an attention-grabbing texturized condensed sans, sure to leave a lasting impression,' aiming for 'a visceral, almost tactile response.'

name: Zuume Soft
classification_notes: The rounded-corner member of the Zuume family, keeping the same condensed, upright stance but softening every corner.
summary: A rounded, condensed sans from the Zuume family, upright in stance but soft at every corner.
description: Zuume Soft keeps Zuume's upright condensed proportions but rounds off every corner, running Extra Light to Black for magazine headlines, kids' book covers and festival posters.
foundry_blurb: The foundry calls Zuume Soft 'charismatically dichotomous — staunchly upright in its stance, but round where corners should exist,' positioned for 'playful drama' from delicate to impactful weights.
